authority: Infinity System Convergence Standard sections 2, 5, 6, and 8

terms.meaning: A human being, independent of credentials, products, roles, businesses, and public presentation.
currentEvidence: TradeScout shared/schema.ts: users mixes login data, personal data, role state, active business/profile state, consent preferences, and referral ownership.
MealScout shared/schema/legacy.ts: users mixes login data, personal data, user type, product context, affiliate state, subscriptions, and public-profile settings.
terms.migrationRule: Preserve product user IDs as source identifiers; do not treat either product row as the ecosystem person record without reconciliation and consent proof.

terms.meaning: A credential and security boundary through which a person or service authenticates to a product.
currentEvidence: Both products store authentication and person/profile attributes in tables named users.
MealScout users.tradescoutId is a cross-product link beside MealScout-local authentication fields.
terms.migrationRule: Separate authentication linkage from person, role, business, profile, and commercial state before account convergence.

terms.meaning: A person's scoped participation in one Infinity product, including status and product roles.
currentEvidence: TradeScout stores role, roles, activeRole, and participationModes on users.
MealScout stores one userType and appContext on users.
terms.migrationRule: Model product participation as a relationship; a product role must not redefine the person or authentication account.

terms.meaning: An organization or commercial operator that can exist before it is claimed and can have owners, staff, locations, and product-specific capabilities.
currentEvidence: TradeScout shared/schema.ts: businesses is a first-class, claimable record decoupled from users.
MealScout shared/schema/legacy.ts: restaurants also represents bars and food trucks; suppliers and hosts use separate owner-bearing tables.
terms.migrationRule: Retain restaurant, food-truck, supplier, and host behavior as product modules while mapping their organizational identity through one business boundary.

terms.meaning: A public or private presentation of a person or business within a product; it is not the identity or ownership record.
currentEvidence: TradeScout userProfiles represents participation intent and verification while profiles represents public website pages.
MealScout uses publicProfileSettings on users plus driverProfiles and workerProfiles for specialized product presentations.
terms.migrationRule: Name profile kinds explicitly and require every profile to reference its subject and product context.

terms.meaning: A scoped participation or authorization assignment; it is not a human type or business type.
currentEvidence: TradeScout uses role, roles, activeRole, roleContext, userIntent, and profile business type across user, business, and profile records.
MealScout userType combines customer participation, business/operator type, staff status, and administrative authority.
terms.migrationRule: Separate product role, business membership role, occupation/presentation, and privileged administrative authorization.

terms.meaning: A relationship granting a person scoped participation in a business, group, property, or product with an explicit lifecycle.
currentEvidence: TradeScout contains accelerator, group, HOA, and procurement workspace memberships.
MealScout businessStaffMemberships grants permissions only in the restaurant-scoped business model.
terms.migrationRule: Keep membership types separate while sharing subject, scope, role, permission, status, provenance, and lifecycle semantics.

terms.meaning: A consented relationship or communication permission between subjects, distinct from a recommendation, follow, assignment, or transaction.
currentEvidence: TradeScout contactPermissions records requester, target, intent, authority gate, decision scope, and status.
TradeScout also has follows, professional partnerships, lead assignments, and conversation membership with different meanings.
terms.migrationRule: Do not collapse social follows, contact consent, business membership, assignments, and partnerships into one generic connection row.

terms.meaning: A typed expression of intent asking another subject or system for an outcome.
currentEvidence: TradeScout has workRequests, verificationRequests, profileBookingRequests, marketplaceInquiries, and service requests.
MealScout has supplierRequests, locationRequests, verificationRequests, payout requests, and private-chef leads.
terms.migrationRule: Share request envelope semantics only; keep payload, authority, state machine, and owner with the product capability that fulfills the request.

terms.meaning: A work opportunity or accepted unit of labor with parties, scope, lifecycle, and compensation terms.
currentEvidence: TradeScout distinguishes tasks, employment posts, work requests, and commercial project bids.
MealScout distinguishes deliveryJobs from restaurant jobPosts and their separate applications.
terms.migrationRule: Do not merge job tables by name; first identify the shared lifecycle and the product-specific work contract.

terms.meaning: A bounded initiative with an owner, scope, lifecycle, and optional plans, documents, bids, or milestones.
currentEvidence: TradeScout has homeProjects and commercialProjects with different owners, states, documents, plans, and bidding behavior.
terms.migrationRule: Share project vocabulary and references without forcing home and commercial workflows into one lifecycle.

terms.meaning: A real-world place or real-estate subject; ownership, participation, condition records, projects, and listings are relationships or projections around it.
currentEvidence: TradeScout has userHomes, propertyPrograms, propertyParticipants, listings, records, lifecycle events, and readiness snapshots.
terms.migrationRule: Select one durable property identity before joining homeowner records, listings, service history, or participant permissions.

terms.meaning: A durable owned or managed object such as a vehicle or equipment item, distinct from its records, documents, listings, and transactions.
currentEvidence: TradeScout userVehicles separates the vehicle from records and documents; other inventory and listing records use their own identities.
terms.migrationRule: Introduce a shared asset reference only when two real consumers require it; retain product-specific attributes and lifecycles.

terms.meaning: A non-binding expected price or effort prepared before an agreement; it is not a quote, invoice, authorization, or payment.
currentEvidence: TradeScout stores pricing data for quote calculators and has conversation-scoped quotes.
MealScout uses preparation estimates but has no inspected shared commercial estimate owner.
terms.migrationRule: Do not alias estimate, quote, bid, invoice, and payment; approve their transitions and binding effect first.

terms.meaning: An authorized movement of money against an obligation; it is separate from attribution, evidence, pricing, rewards, credits, and payout requests.
currentEvidence: TradeScout has contractor payments, marketplace transactions, wallet transactions, donations, and support ledgers.
MealScout has pickup payments, host earnings, commissions, credits, withdrawals, settlements, and payout requests.
terms.migrationRule: Keep execution product-owned until policy, authorization, idempotency, reconciliation, and ledger ownership are approved per flow.

terms.meaning: A time-bound decision about a specific subject and claim, backed by evidence and an accountable reviewer or provider.
currentEvidence: TradeScout stores verification state on users and userProfiles and in business, vendor, buyer, address, identity, and document records.
MealScout stores email and business verification booleans alongside verification requests, insurance review, identity views, and ordering approval.
terms.migrationRule: Never promote a generic verified boolean across claim types; require subject, claim, evidence, method, decision, reviewer, and expiry.
